title: Does Literal-Match Reranker Supervision Improve Generated Answers in RAG? An In-Domain and Transfer Study
authors: Assylkhan Geniyat, Zukhriddin Fakhriddinov, Atharv Gulati
abstract: Rerankers decide which passages a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system shows to its generator, and adapting them requires relevance labels. Document-level labels come free with question-answer data but are coarse: they mark every passage of the correct document as relevant, even when it lacks the answer. Labels that instead reward passages containing the reference answer verbatim look more precise. We put this literal-match supervision to a controlled test, with a fixed generator and a success criterion set in advance: a statistically significant gain of at least one point in answer F1 (word overlap with the reference answer). In neither study does it deliver that gain. On 208 held-out TechQA technical-support questions, it improves passage ranking over hybrid retrieval, but the answer gain is not significant (+0.68 points). Under transfer to support dialogues (Doc2Dial), it ranks evidence worse than document-level labels and gives slightly lower answer F1 (-0.22 points); for the trained adapters, the targeted gain is ruled out. A second finding holds across both studies: clear differences in retrieval quality barely move answer F1, which also tracks response length. Retrieval metrics are therefore an unreliable guide here, and reranker supervision should be judged by the answers it produces, using an answer metric shown to detect retrieval changes.
